replacements.headText: The stores will carry the town through hunger. Nothing here will carry it through a plague, and the town has not built anything that would.
replacements.was: The stores carry the town through hunger. Nothing here carries it through a plague, and the town has built nothing that would.
replacements.now: The stores can carry the town through hunger. Nothing here can carry it through a plague, and the town has built nothing that would.
replacements.ground: At HEAD both clauses read "will carry", which is dispositional: if hunger comes the stores suffice, and if plague comes nothing here does. Bare present "carry"/"carries" is ambiguous between that and a habitual reading (hunger recurs at this settlement and the store is routinely drawn down) which the card, whose state is grain store PRESENT and asserts nothing about recurring famine, does not license, so under 42b the cut line makes no claim a reader can act on; "can" in both clauses puts HEAD's capability claim back in this pool's own word for it at HEAD ("can feed itself", "can outlast a hungry year"), is on no bar list, and keeps every gain of the cut (both "will" bars stay gone, and "has built nothing" stays in place of "has not built anything", the same claim in a better shape).

replacements.headText: The town can outlast a hungry year at {settlement} and has no answer at all to a sick one, and knows which of the two it fears.
replacements.was: The town can outlast a hungry year at {settlement} and has no answer at all to a sick one. It is the sick year the town fears.
replacements.now: The town can outlast a hungry year at {settlement} and has no answer at all to a sick one. The town knows the sick year is the one it fears.
replacements.ground: The cut's new sentence dropped a HEAD claim as well as adding one: HEAD asserted that the town KNOWS which of the two it fears, which licenses a game master to stage a townsperson answering that question straight, and "It is the sick year the town fears" says nothing about the town's settled self-knowledge. Restoring "knows" costs no clarity and puts that half of the delta back, while 42b still forbids returning to HEAD's vague tail, so the definite "the sick year" stays, the split into two sentences stays (the second carries a real fact and so earns its place under 42a), and the line is also listed under sharpenings42b with the full two-way delta for the refuter.

sharpenings42b.headText: The town can outlast a hungry year at {settlement} and has no answer at all to a sick one, and knows which of the two it fears.
sharpenings42b.nowText: The town can outlast a hungry year at {settlement} and has no answer at all to a sick one. The town knows the sick year is the one it fears.
sharpenings42b.readingChosen: Of the two years named, it is the sick one the town fears, and the town knows it.
sharpenings42b.whyThePoolStateSupportsIt: HEAD's tail names no fear and so makes no claim a reader can act on, the textbook 42b failure, and the pool's own state settles which reading is lawful: the grain store is present, so a failed harvest is survivable, and there is no medical provision of any kind, so of the two years named in the same sentence only the sick one is uncovered. The alternative reading would contradict the first half of its own sentence. The line as repaired hands the refuter the WHOLE delta rather than half of it: the sharpening ADDS which year is feared, and my repair RESTORES the town's knowledge of it, so the refuter must test both, and in particular whether the card supports attributing a fear, and knowledge of that fear, to the town as a body at all rather than only the two capability facts.

declined.faceOrSpine: SPINE variant 1 [ledger]
declined.why: The auditor's SHOULD_FIX RULING_42a_BREACH would delete "A sickness here spreads until it stops of its own accord.", a sentence HEAD carries in full. That deletion is itself claim movement and the freeze wins: "has nothing at all against disease" is an absence of PROVISION, while the second sentence says what actually happens, that a sickness runs unchecked and nobody intervenes even informally. The auditor's own least-sure concedes exactly this reading and concedes the fix loses a fact on it, and the adversary's overturn in variant 2 settled the governing principle for this neighbourhood from the engine's own prose, that provision here arrives either as a building or as a person, so an absence of one does not entail the absence of the other. The cut's only change to this line was semicolon to full stop, which clears a hard mechanical bar at no claim cost, so the line stands as cut. If the chair wants the clarity question reopened it belongs to D1's chartered car, off the freeze.

declined.faceOrSpine: SPINE variant 2 [unfolding]
declined.why: The auditor's SHOULD_FIX RULING_42_BREACH and its fix ("The stores carry the town through hunger. The town has built nothing that would carry it through a plague.") is declined, as the adversary overturned it and the chair's section A and C do not cover it. The two halves are two facts, not one twice: the fix drops the general capability-absence and keeps only the construction-absence, which licenses a game master to believe an unbuilt answer, a person or the tending, might still exist in a pool whose state is NO medical provision. That is a moved claim introduced by the audit rather than by the cut.

declined.faceOrSpine: SPINE variant 3 [street]
declined.why: Restoring HEAD's exact tail, "and knows which of the two it fears", is declined. It names no fear, so it fails 42b, and it is a trailing third clause chained by a second "and", which is the shape 42 bans. The repair therefore keeps the split and the definite year and restores only the dropped "knows".

declined.faceOrSpine: POOL (header) and all three variants
declined.why: The zero-face state is not line work and is not mine. The adversary settled it with receipts on both revisions, zero face lines at HEAD and zero in the inflight tree, the face-count register unmoved and mkpools.py's FACE COUNT MOVED guard correctly silent, against siblings carrying fifteen to thirty-five. It is a pre-existing coverage hole already chartered by the chair at D3 as the block's last unwritten work, so I neither wrote faces nor touched the header.

declined.faceOrSpine: SPINE (all three variants), SHAPE_MONOTONY
declined.why: No D2 shape conversion is available in this pool, so I took none. All three variants run the same figure (copes with hunger, no answer to sickness, then a tail on the pair), but the only cure is restructuring, which the freeze bars, and the three lines are already bare engine facts with no speaker to convert, which is the shape D2 asks for. The note belongs to whoever next holds these lines without the freeze on.

result.summary: Two of the three spines are repaired and one stands; there are no faces in this pool to work. Variant 2 is the real breach: the cut correctly removed both hard "will" bars but left bare present in both clauses, which is ambiguous between HEAD's dispositional claim and a habitual reading that licenses recurring famine and a routinely drawn-down store, a fact the card (grain store PRESENT) never asserts, so both clauses now read "can", which is this pool's own word for the same capability at HEAD in variants 1 and 3 and is on no bar list; every other gain of the cut is kept. Variant 3's 42b sharpening is lawful and stays, but the cut had also DROPPED a HEAD claim, that the town knows which of the two it fears, so "knows" is restored at no clarity cost and the line is listed under sharpenings42b with the full two-way delta rather than half of it. Variant 1 stands as cut: its only change was semicolon to full stop, which moves no claim, and the auditor's 42a deletion of its second sentence is declined because it would drop HEAD's fact that a sickness here runs unchecked with nobody intervening even informally, a reading the auditor's own least-sure concedes and the adversary's variant 2 overturn establishes for this neighbourhood. Both repaired lines were scanned by execution against every mechanical bar and every 42c word and are clean, and no line from the frozen `granary AND hospital` pair appears anywhere in this output. Nothing here needed constraint (i) or (ii): no line in this pool contains "the elders say", "granary" or "infirmary", so no provenance cure and no grain-store substitution was in play, and I added no object to any spine.

replacements.headText: Those who keep the ground say the same words go over the house that gives everything and the house that gives nothing.
replacements.was: Those who keep the ground say they speak the same words over the house that gives everything and the house that gives nothing.
replacements.now: Those who keep the ground say the same words go over the house that gives everything and the house that gives nothing.
replacements.ground: HEAD says the same words go over both houses without naming who speaks them, so a local priest could be the one officiating and the line still hold; the cut makes the ground-keepers the speakers, which is a new fact about who performs a burying rite and is the chair's own A-class shape of an unnamed actor becoming a named one. The stake could only be bought with that actor, so under the collision rule the freeze wins; HEAD already carries 42c's sanctioned wording for the source and has no trailing clause, so the repair is HEAD verbatim and no clarity gain is lost. The auditor filed this face as the clean model and the adversary caught it, correctly.

replacements.headText: At the drinking house they say one house gives the word and another takes the work.
replacements.was: At the tavern the men who take the work say one house gives the word and another does it.
replacements.now: At the tavern they say one house gives the word and another takes the work.
replacements.ground: Two things moved. The speaker went from the tavern crowd reporting on two houses from outside to the labouring house's own men reporting their own grievance, a class the tavern source is not on its card and which makes the sentence report in the third person on the very work its speakers say they do; and "another does it" leaves "it" able to attach to the word as easily as to the work, which HEAD's "takes the work" did not. Both the speaker and the object go back to HEAD, and the one gain that costs no claim, the 42c swap from drinking house to tavern, is kept. 42d is left unmet here rather than met by an invented speaker class.

replacements.headText: A pedlar says a visitor here learns whose door answers for what before learning anybody's name.
replacements.was: A travelling trader says he learns whose door answers for what here before he learns anybody's name.
replacements.now: A travelling trader says he learns here whose door answers for what before learning anybody's name.
replacements.ground: Nothing in the claim moves from the cut line: the 42c swap the brief names by hand and the speaker-in-his-own-sentence stake both stay, and the tense stays habitual so the chair's A1 lets that stake stand. What is repaired is wording only. "Here" had drifted to the end of "whose door answers for what here", where it reads as a stumble, so it moves back beside the verb it modifies, and HEAD's own "before learning anybody's name" comes back in place of the repeated "he learns". The narrowing from all visitors to this trader survives and is listed as a sharpening for re-refutation against the stranger card.

replacements.headText: The heads of the households hold that what is given here is given outright.
replacements.was: The heads of the households hold that what they give here is given outright.
replacements.now: The heads of the households hold that what is given here is given outright.
replacements.ground: "What is given here" is a claim about all giving in the place; "what they give here" restricts it to the household heads' own giving, which is the chair's A3 shape of a general subject narrowed to the speakers, and it shrinks pair 1, since the tavern half still asserts about all giving. The stake was bought with that narrowing and by nothing else, so the freeze wins and HEAD comes back verbatim. HEAD needs no 42c work and has no trailing clause, so the repair costs no gain.

replacements.headText: At the drinking house they say what is given here is remembered by the giver longer than by the taker.
replacements.was: At the tavern they say what is given here is remembered longer by the giver than by the taker. Both sit at the same table.
replacements.now: At the tavern they say what is given here is remembered longer by the giver than by the taker.
replacements.ground: "Both sit at the same table." is a whole sentence of fact that appears in no WAS line, asserting that giver and taker drink together, and it fails 42a on its own test, since deleting it leaves the first sentence missing nothing. It is cut. The 42c swap to tavern and the tightened comparison order are kept, and the claim left standing is HEAD's.

replacements.headText: The muster's account is that what reaches it first is the shouting, and that the shouting is enough to go on.
replacements.was: The muster reckons what reaches it first is the shouting, and the shouting is enough to go on.
replacements.now: The muster's account is that what reaches it first is the shouting, and that the shouting is enough to go on.
replacements.ground: Dropping the parallel "that" lets the second clause escape the attribution, so on one available reading the engine vouches bare that shouting really is enough to go on, which is a fact about the settlement's readiness rather than a muster opinion a game master can play as complacent and wrong; two readings now fit, which is a 42b breach in any case. "The muster's account is that" also became "The muster reckons", turning a report the muster has given into an opinion it holds, and on a pool whose machinery turns on witnesses and the record those are different facts. HEAD is restored whole, which re-joins the attribution and keeps the wording the classifier has already measured; no owner ruling asked for the shorter verb, so nothing is lost.

sharpenings42b.headText: A drover says a house here lends a thing for the asking. What comes back is a different thing of about the same use.
sharpenings42b.nowText: A drover says a house here lends him a thing for the asking. What comes back is a different thing of about the same use.
sharpenings42b.readingChosen: The drover is himself a borrower under the custom, not only a reporter of it.
sharpenings42b.whyThePoolStateSupportsIt: Left in place. The pronoun insertion is 42d's named method, the tense stays habitual present, and the chair's A1 allows a stake that can be carried in the present tense; the custom's own content, that a house lends for the asking and a different thing of about the same use comes back, is word for word HEAD's. The pool has strangers transacting on these terms already, with a traveller being quoted a price at variant 1 face 1 and a stranger's pack weighed at the way through at variant 2 face 3, so the reading is consistent with the pool's state. What it is not is covered by the standing refutation, because HEAD alleged a local custom and the cut commits the drover to having borrowed under it, so whether the stranger card grants him a borrowing is the open card question.

sharpenings42b.headText: A pedlar says a visitor here learns whose door answers for what before learning anybody's name.
sharpenings42b.nowText: A travelling trader says he learns here whose door answers for what before learning anybody's name.
sharpenings42b.readingChosen: The trader reports his own repeated experience of the place rather than a rule about every visitor.
sharpenings42b.whyThePoolStateSupportsIt: The repair above is word order only, so the sharpening stands and needs refuting. HEAD claimed that any visitor learns the doors before the names; the cut claims it of this trader. The habitual present keeps it inside A1's allowance, and the pool supports a stranger reporting his own case, with a traveller reporting his own treatment at variant 1 face 1 and the gate sizing strangers up one at a time at variant 2 face 3. The card should confirm the trader has been here more than once, since "he learns" is habitual rather than a single visit.

result.summary: All seven changed faces in Economic Survival: CRITICAL are ruled, and the three spines are untouched as the table records. Six replacements: variant 1 face 4 and variant 3 face 2 go back to HEAD verbatim because both bought a 42d stake by moving who acts, the ground-keepers made the speakers of the words at a burying and the household heads made the only givers, which are the chair's A4 and A3 shapes and are exactly the collision the freeze wins; variant 2 face 4 goes back to the tavern crowd and to "takes the work", keeping only the 42c swap, since the cut installed a speaker class that is not on the tavern card and left "it" ambiguous; variant 3 face 3 loses the added sentence "Both sit at the same table." and keeps the 42c swap and the tightened comparison; variant 3 face 6 goes back to HEAD whole, because the dropped parallel "that" stranded the second clause on the engine and "reckons" downgraded a report on the record to an opinion held; variant 3 face 1 takes a word-order repair only, moving "here" back beside its verb and restoring HEAD's "before learning anybody's name". Two lines are left in place as lawful 42b sharpenings for re-refutation against the stranger card, the drover who now borrows for the asking and the travelling trader who now reports his own learning, both habitual present and so inside the chair's A1 allowance. Nothing is taken from D2, because the adversary showed all three proposed shape conversions turn a role's allegation into an engine-held fact, and D1's untouched faces are left to the chartered car. No mechanical bar is tripped in any repaired line, no repair introduces "The elders say", no grain store wording exists in this pool, and neither frozen line is in it.

replacements.headText: A clerk in the hall says the store is the town's to keep and not the town's to open.
replacements.was: A clerk in the hall says the store the hall keeps is the town's, and not the town's to open.
replacements.now: A clerk in the hall says the store is the town's to keep and not the town's to open.
replacements.ground: The cut split one undifferentiated fact into two by naming the hall as the keeper and leaving the town only the owning, which is the chair's A4 instance 'the town -> the hall as keeper'. Restoring HEAD's actor also dissolves the sharpening the adversary wanted collected, so this face owes no new refutation.

replacements.headText: Those who sell at the market say the store takes no part in the price of the loaf.
replacements.was: Those who sell at the market reckon the store takes no part in the price of the loaf.
replacements.now: Those who sell at the market say the store takes no part in the price of the loaf.
replacements.ground: At HEAD the market people state the fact; 'reckon' makes it an estimate they hold, so what a game master may rely on moves without any wording of the fact changing. 'Reckon' is also regional register rather than a plain modern word, so the swap fails the rule it was reaching for.

replacements.headText: A local priest says the store has a door and a lock. The tending has neither.
replacements.was: A local priest has it that the store has a door and a lock. The tending has neither.
replacements.now: A local priest says the store has a door and a lock. The tending has neither.
replacements.ground: 'Has it that' is a fusty attribution formula that 42c withdrew the licence for, and it downgrades the priest from a man stating a fact to a channel for hearsay, which weakens the attribution the freeze protects. HEAD was already at the standard, so HEAD's verb goes back and its two-sentence shape is kept.

replacements.headText: The guilds say the store is no use to a man who cannot work, and the trades carry that loss themselves.
replacements.was: The guilds hold that the store is no use to a man who cannot work, and the trades carry that loss themselves.
replacements.now: The guilds say the store is no use to a man who cannot work, and the trades carry that loss themselves.
replacements.ground: 'Hold that' converts an asserted fact into a position the guilds take, which moves the fact's standing, and it re-inserts the subordinator the rest of the cut spent its edits removing. HEAD's plain 'say' costs nothing to restore.

replacements.headText: One of those on the gate says a cart carrying for the store goes through ahead of a cart carrying for a stall.
replacements.was: One of those on the gate reports that a cart carrying for the store goes through ahead of a cart carrying for a stall.
replacements.now: One of those on the gate says a cart carrying for the store goes through ahead of a cart carrying for a stall.
replacements.ground: 'Reports that' is longer, more bureaucratic and less plain than HEAD's 'says', and it puts back the 'that' the cut removed six times elsewhere. The auditor's DOES-shape alternative is not taken here because it would make one gateman the actor of a practice HEAD states generally.

replacements.headText: The garrison says the store is the one thing here worth standing in front of, and that standing in front of it is nobody's order.
replacements.was: The garrison says the store is the one thing here worth standing in front of, and nobody has ordered it to.
replacements.now: The garrison says the store is the one thing here worth standing in front of, and nobody has ordered the garrison to stand there.
replacements.ground: The cut left 'it' with the store as its nearest noun and elided the infinitive after 'to', which the adversary settled as a copy edit rather than a 42b breach. Naming the addressee and the act fixes the infelicity but keeps the cut's narrowing of HEAD's scope-vague 'nobody's order', so the claim is not identical and the face is listed for separate refutation.

replacements.headText: Everyone here has seen the store door and nobody here has seen it stand open, and everyone here knows that a sickness in a house is answered by whoever the parish sends.
replacements.was: Everyone here has seen the store door and nobody here has seen it stand open. A sickness in a house is answered by whoever the parish sends.
replacements.now: Everyone here has seen the store door and nobody here has seen it stand open. Everyone here knows a sickness in a house is answered by whoever the parish sends.
replacements.ground: The split is a real clarity gain and both sentences carry a fact, but it stranded 'everyone here knows', so under ruling 40 the engine now vouches bare for what the street vouched for. The knower is put back inside the second sentence and the 'that' stays out, so the split survives and the attribution returns.

replacements.headText: At the tavern they say the one who comes to sit up and the one who comes to dig are the same trade.
replacements.was: At the tavern they say the man who sits up with a drinker and the man who digs for him are the same trade.
replacements.now: At the tavern they say the one who comes to sit up and the one who comes to dig are the same trade.
replacements.ground: Two of the chair's A4 instances are in this one line: the tended shrank from anybody to the tavern's own drinker, and 'the one who' became 'the man who' twice, asserting a sex HEAD declines to assert where the parish's tender is 'whoever the parish sends'. The 42d stake cannot be carried without the fact, so under the collision rule the stake is given up and HEAD's own words go back.

replacements.headText: Those who sell at the market say a household with somebody ill in it comes late and buys small, and that the stalls know a sick house sooner than the parish.
replacements.was: Those who sell at the market say a household with somebody ill in it comes late and buys small. The stalls know a sick house sooner than the parish.
replacements.now: Those who sell at the market say a household with somebody ill in it comes late and buys small, and the stalls know a sick house sooner than the parish.
replacements.ground: The second fact sat inside 'say ... and that ...'; the full stop left it self-standing with no back-reference, so by ruling 40 the engine itself now asserts that the stalls do know before the parish, when HEAD licensed only that the market people say so. Re-joining it as a coordinated clause holds the reported-speech frame and keeps the 'that' deletion.

replacements.headText: A traveller says that asking after the sick here gets a person and asking after the grain gets a building.
replacements.was: A traveller says he asked after the sick here and was given a person, and asked after the grain and was given a building.
replacements.now: A traveller says that asking after the sick here gets a person and asking after the grain gets a building.
replacements.ground: HEAD states a habit that meets anyone who asks; the cut turned it into one episode in one traveller's past, which is the chair's A1 class exactly. The stake here can only be carried in the past tense, so the claim wins and the stake is given up. HEAD's wording is restored intact because dropping its 'that' before a gerund subject reads worse, not plainer.

replacements.headText: A local priest says a stranger asks for a house and is given a person, and that nobody born here asks for the house.
replacements.was: A local priest says a stranger asks for a house and is sent him instead, and nobody born here asks for a house at all.
replacements.now: A local priest says a stranger asks for a house and is given a person, and nobody born here asks for the house.
replacements.ground: 'Is sent him' moves the giving onto the speaking priest and parses two ways, so by 42b it makes no claim, and 'a house at all' widens off the house the stranger asked for. HEAD's unnamed giver and HEAD's back-reference both return, while the 'and that' deletion the cut made is kept.

replacements.headText: At the tavern they say strangers walk up to look at the store, and that nobody here does.
replacements.was: At the tavern they say strangers walk up to look at the store, and no drinker there has ever bothered.
replacements.now: At the tavern they say strangers walk up to look at the store, and nobody here does.
replacements.ground: The chair's A3 names this instance: 'nobody here' means the town and 'no drinker there' means one room of it. Two further riders came in with it, an imputed indifference in 'bothered' and a perfect tense covering all past time, and restoring HEAD's clause undoes all three at once. The auditor's 'nobody in the town' is not taken because it is a sharpening that would owe fresh refutation, where HEAD's words owe none.

replacements.headText: A guild factor says what a stranger takes for provision is a store the trades filled and cannot open.
replacements.was: A guild member reckons what a stranger takes for provision is a store the trades filled and cannot open.
replacements.now: A guild member says what a stranger takes for provision is a store the trades filled and cannot open.
replacements.ground: The 42c swap from factor to member is the owner's own word and is kept, matching the same swap left standing at variant 2 face 5. 'Reckons' downgrades the stated fact to an estimate, so HEAD's 'says' returns; the de-inversion the auditor proposed is left for the chartered car.

sharpenings42b.headText: The garrison says the store is the one thing here worth standing in front of, and that standing in front of it is nobody's order.

sharpenings42b.readingChosen: No order to stand in front of the store has been given to the garrison. The wider reading HEAD's 'nobody's order' also carried, that no such order exists for anybody at all, is dropped.
sharpenings42b.whyThePoolStateSupportsIt: The garrison is the only armed body on any card in this pool, so an order to stand in front of the store would fall to it, and the face is sourced [garrison]. The adversary overturned the 42b vagueness charge on this line but upheld the narrowing as real, so the sharpening is left in place and collected: it asserts something about the garrison's own orders that HEAD's scope-vague clause did not, and the standing refutation does not reach it.
